blocks.title: Job aid for COVID-19 vaccine Administration
Janssen–Cilag International NV (Belgium) Ad26.COV2.S COVID-19 vaccine
blocks.content: (International non-proprietary name: Ad26.COV2.S COVID-19 Vaccine)

summary.text: Gives the international non-proprietary name of the Janssen Ad26.COV2.S COVID-19 vaccine covered by this job aid.

blocks.title: General information
blocks.content:
GENERAL INFORMATION 
 Vaccine: Janssen Ad26.COV2.S COVID-19 vaccine, multi-dose vial. Each vial contains 5 doses of 0.5 ml 
 Schedule: One dose of 0.5 ml 
 Age indication: 18 years of age and older 
 
 Route and site of administration: Intramuscular, in the deltoid muscle of the upper arm

summary.text: Summarises key facts on the Janssen COVID-19 vaccine: five-dose vials, a single 0.5 ml dose, use from age 18 and intramuscular injection in the deltoid.

blocks.title: Storage conditionS and shelf life of vaccine
blocks.content:
STORAGE CONDITIONS AND SHELF LIFE OF VACCINE 
STORAGE CONDITIONS SHELF LIFE 
 
Unopened vaccine vials: 
Freezer: -25 °C to -15 °C 
24 months by expiry date 
• Prior to use, avoid vaccine exposure to direct sunlight and 
ultraviolet light. 
• Do NOT refreeze the vaccine, once thawed. 
Refrigerator: +2 °C to +8 °C 
Up to 4.5 months  
(not exceeding expiry date) 
Opened vial (after first puncture of the vial) *: 
• During use, vaccines can be handled in room light conditions.  
• Punctured vaccine vials should be discarded within 6 hours 
after first puncturing OR at the end of the immunization

summary.text: Sets out storage conditions and shelf life for the Janssen COVID-19 vaccine, frozen for up to 24 months or refrigerated for up to 4.5 months, and stresses protection from light and no refreezing after thawing. It explains that opened vials must be used within six hours or by the end of the session, and how to record dates and update expiry dates when moving vials to the refrigerator.

blocks.title: Thawing of frozen vaccine:
blocks.content:
• 
Frozen vaccine vials may be thawed in the refrigerator (between +2 °C to +8 °C) This will take approximately 2 hours for a single 
vial and 12 hours for a carton of 10 vials. 

 NOTE: Do NOT refreeze thawed vaccine.

summary.text: Explains that frozen vials can be thawed in the refrigerator, taking about two hours for one vial and twelve for a carton, and must not be refrozen.

blocks.content:

Hand hygiene (alcohol-based hand rub or running water and soa

summary.text: Lists supplies needed for vaccination, including suitable syringes and needles, antiseptic swabs, a sharps box, anaphylaxis kits, personal protective equipment and hand hygiene materials.

blocks.title: Contraindications and precautions for vaccination
blocks.content: CONTRAINDICATIONS AND PRECAUTIONS FOR VACCINATION

summary.text: A heading introducing the contraindications and precautions for the Janssen COVID-19 vaccine.

blocks.title: Contraindications:
blocks.content:
• 
History of severe allergic reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis) to any component of the vaccine.

summary.text: States the single contraindication: a history of severe allergic reaction to any vaccine component.

blocks.title: Precautions:
blocks.content:
• 
Acute febrile illness 
• 
Individuals receiving anticoagulant therapy or those with thrombocytopenia or any coagulation disorder (such as haemophilia) 
because bleeding or bruising may occur following an intramuscular administration

blocks.title: Preparation and administration of vaccine
blocks.content:
PREPARATION AND ADMINISTRATION OF VACCINE 

 NOTE: The thawed vaccine is ready to use. Do NOT dilute the vaccine. Do NOT freeze the vaccine, once thawed. 
PREPARATION FOR VACCINE ADMINISTRATION ENVIRONMENT 
1 
 
• Be sure to wear correct personal protective equipment (PPE) before administering vaccines. Ensure that 
the implemented policies for the use of face coverings for vaccine recipients are in place. 
2 
 
• Assess recipient status: 

 Screen for contraindications and precautions (see above). 

 Review vaccination history: Has any other vaccine been administered within the previous 14

summary.text: Gives step-by-step instructions for preparing and giving the Janssen vaccine, from wearing protective equipment and screening the recipient (including a 14-day gap after other vaccines) to aseptic withdrawal of a 0.5 ml dose without dilution. It covers injecting into the deltoid, observing the person afterwards, recording the date, name and batch number, and reporting suspected adverse reactions.

blocks.title: Management of anaphylaxis and anxiety-related reactions
blocks.content:
MANAGEMENT OF ANAPHYLAXIS AND ANXIETY-RELATED REACTIONS
Events of anaphylaxis and anxiety-related reactions may occur. Make sure that a health-care worker competent in identifying and 
treating these reactions, and necessary equipment and medications, are available. Take precautions to avoid injury from fainting.

summary.text: Advises that staff, equipment and medicines to manage anaphylaxis and anxiety-related reactions be on hand, with precautions against injury from fainting.

blocks.title: Communication during vaccination visit
blocks.content:
COMMUNICATION DURING VACCINATION VISIT
1 
Explain the benefits of the vaccine 
“The COVID-19 vaccine is a safe way to protect yourself from the COVID-19 (coronavirus) disease.” 
2 
Enquire about and screen for contraindications and precautions 
“We want to make sure it will be safe for you to receive the vaccine.” [Ask about the contraindications and precautions listed 
above.] 
3 
Explain the process 
“The vaccine is given through an injection into the upper arm. You may feel a slight pinch when the needle goes in. 
Afterwards, we want you to stay here for 15 minutes to be sure you don’t have

summary.text: Sets out suggested wording for the vaccination visit, covering vaccine benefits, screening questions, how the injection is given, the 15-minute observation period and common side effects. It also offers sample answers to typical concerns about side effects and conflicting information.
